## Natural history notes

A native evergreen to semi-evergreen woody vine characterized by glossy opposite leaves and fragrant, bright yellow trumpet-shaped flowers that bloom primarily in late winter and spring. Yellow Jessamine occurs throughout much of Florida in pine flatwoods, hammocks, woodland edges, thickets, and along fences and roadsides, where it climbs over shrubs and small trees. Its early flowers provide nectar for pollinating insects, but all parts of the plant contain toxic alkaloids and can be poisonous if ingested. It is also widely cultivated as an ornamental vine because of its showy flowers and vigorous growth.
